newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch say no decision yet on extra EU summit.
newsitem.headline: Dutch say no decision yet on extra EU summit.

text.p: No decision has yet been taken on whether the Dutch presidency of the European Union will schedule an extraordinary summit in Maastricht in May, a Dutch government official said on Friday.

Hans van der Ploeg, spokesman for Dutch Prime Minister Wim Kok, told a press briefing a decision on the mooted Maastricht summit would most likely be taken at a meeting of EU foreign ministers in Luxembourg on April 29 and 30.
The Dutch Foreign Ministry has cited May 23 as the most likely date for a special summit.
Finnish news agency STT on Friday reported EU sources in Brussels had said the Netherlands was expected to announce the decision on the summit during the course of the day.
Kok signalled in early March that a special summit was being considered ahead of a scheduled Amsterdam meeting on June 16 and 17.
EU leaders are then due to agree a new treaty, paving the way for accession talks with a number of ex-communist states from eastern Europe.

The year-long intergovernmental conference (IGC), aimed at wide-ranging treaty reforms to prepare the union for the expansion process, has become bogged down over how to reshape the executive Commission and ensure fair weighting to member states' votes in the decision-making process.
